notes: D1 oracle for this city is thinner than its Oslo/Rotterdam/Newcastle siblings: no official passenger map or timetable was transcribed (PDF blocked by egress policy). Station names are hand-transcribed from Trafiklab GTFS Regional `skane` stops.txt only. Line-level structure (termini, ordered stops, branches, confirmed line codes) is NOT in the oracle report and is NOT populated in this file — see coverageGaps and lines[] below.

Scope correction from the expansion tracker: tracker lists Malmö as 'commuter + light rail (Skånetrafiken)'. Malmö has no active light rail/tram system — the historical tram network closed in 1973; only a seasonal (Sat/Sun) museum tram remains, which is not v1. V1 is Pågatågen commuter rail only.
City id malmo is separate from goteborg (Västtrafik) and from stockholm. Do not merge.

Trafiklab GTFS Regional operator code `skane` confirmed to resolve to Skånetrafiken. Same TRAFIKLAB_API_KEY as Göteborg (different operator code). GTFS-RT (TripUpdates + vehicle positions) confirmed available for `skane`, unlike Göteborg's schedule-only gap — relevant to Jim's D2+ live board, not to this D1 file.

V1 mode cut: Pågatågen only. No Malmö stadsbuss / regional bus, no tram/spårvagn (none active in passenger service), no Öresundståg (separate cross-border operator: Skånetrafiken + DSB + Region Hovedstaden), no X-bus, no coach terminals (e.g. Nils Ericsonsplatsen — that's Göteborg's, not Malmö's; excluded here for clarity that no coach terminal is in scope).

Hub lock Malmö C (Malmö Central Station): City Tunnel (Citytunneln) terminus/portal, opened December 2010; report states 'all or most' Pågatågen lines serve it. doNotGroup Malmö C Pågatågen vs Malmö C Öresundståg (same station, different operator) — the one clash the oracle report confirms directly.

Eleven core Pågatågen lines plus a rush-hour-only line 12, per the oracle report's Oct 2025 line-count claim. This count is stated directly in the report (not hedged as 'presumed'), unlike the specific line codes below, which are hedged. Per-line termini, ordered stops, and branch structure are NOT in the report and are NOT fabricated here.

Line-code format 'H3, H4, E6, etc.' is explicitly flagged in the oracle report as 'expected'/'presumed' and 'must be confirmed in GTFS' — not a confirmed passenger-facing convention. Do not treat these example codes as real line names.
Timezone Europe/Stockholm HAS DST (CEST/CET), same family as Göteborg, Stockholm, Oslo.

gtfsRouteIdsIfKnown / stopIds are deliberately absent from this file, consistent with every sibling D1 pack — those are Jim's D2+ concern against the live feed, not a D1 print lock (and here, unusually, there is no print lock to check them against yet).

coverageGaps: BLOCKING for D5: no per-line termini, ordered stop list, or branch structure exists in the oracle report for any of the 11 regular Pågatågen lines or rush-hour line 12. The lines[] array below is intentionally left as a stub, not populated with invented station arrays — see direction-model-memo.md.
Line-code convention (e.g. whether route_short_name really follows an H3/H4/E6-style pattern) is unconfirmed — oracle report explicitly hedges this.
Whether line 12 is a distinct route_id or a variant trip pattern on an existing line is unconfirmed.
Whether Öresundståg also calls at Triangeln and/or Hyllie (both City Tunnel stations, same corridor as the confirmed Malmö C clash) is unconfirmed.

Malmöringen (ring line) route path is unconfirmed — if any published line calls at Svågertorp, Persborg, or Östervärn twice on one through-path (Oslo line-5-style), inbound/outbound direction labeling will be wrong at that station and this file's direction guidance will need updating.
Burlöv and Oxie inclusion in v1 is conditional per the oracle report itself ('if GTFS includes it') — not independently verified here.

The Skånetrafiken linjenät PDF (dated 1 Dec 2024, for June 2025) that would be the equivalent authority to the Oslo/Rotterdam/Newcastle maps was not accessible (egress policy). No md5/localFile/URL could be confirmed. If this pack is revisited once that source is reachable, station names and line structure should be re-verified against it, not just against GTFS.
Museum tram (seasonal, Sat/Sun) and the 1973 tram closure are out of v1 scope — confirmed, not a gap, listed here only so it isn't mistaken for missing data.
